texts.preamble: State Of Maharashtra vs Prakash Rukman Kotalwar on 15 November, 2019 Author: K.K. Sonawane Bench: K.K. Sonawane {1} Crapl 388.97.odt In The High Court Of Judicature Of Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Criminal Appeal No. 388 Of 1997 The State of Maharashtra through Bhagwat Vithal Bobade Food Inspector, Parbhani District Parbhani. .. Appellant Versus Prakash s/o. Rukman Kotalwar Age 38 yeas, Occ. Business and Prop. M/s. Sadanand Sandip Kotalwar Kirana Shop Bhaji Market Gangakhed, District Parbhani. .. Respondent. Mr. A.A. Jagatkar, App for appellant Mr. R.S. Shinde, Adv. For respondent. Coram : K.K. Sonawane, J. Date : 15Th November, 2019. Oral Judgment:
texts.facts: According to prosecution, the {2} CRAPL 388.97.odt complainant Shri Gopal Pathak was duly appointed as a Food Inspector at the relevant time in the year January 1993. It has been alleged that on 27th January, 1999 at about 4.00 P.M., the complainant Shri Pathak paid visit to the Grocery Shop of the respondent/accused located in Gangakhed town. The complainant Gopal Pathak disclosed his identity as Food Inspector to the respondent/accused and asked him to produce the licence of his shop but the respondent/accused did not produce the same. The complainant Shri Gopal Pathak noticed that there was an item "Badi- saunf" seen kept for sale in the shop. The complainant purchased 600 grams of item Badi-saunf after payment of Rs. 13.20 to the respondent. Thereafter, he gave notice to the respondent in the Form No. VII of the PFA Act and communicated to him that the sample of item Badi-saunf was collected for the purpose of analysis. Thereafter, he issued notice as prescribed under Section 14A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. The purchased item Badi-saunf was kept in the plain and clean paper which was divided in 3 equal parts and thereafter,item Badi-saunf was preserved in 3 clean and empty polythene packets. These polythene packets were sealed and signed by him in the presence of panchas. These samples were wrapped in the thick brown paper with lable on it. After compliance of procedural formalities of seizure and sealing of the item Badi- saunf, the one sample was sent to the public analyst accompanied with the form No. VII with a request to carry out the analysis of the sample. The one sample packet of Badi-saunf was given to the respondent. Meanwhile, the complainant received information from the Licencing Authority that there was no licence granted in favour of respondent-shop owner to run the business of grocery shop for sale of food articles. Thereafter, report of the public analyst was also received from the Local Health Authority which revealed that the sample of item Badi-saunf sent to the public analyst for analysis contained extraneous non-permitted green colour matter. Therefore, {3} CRAPL 388.97.odt it did not conform to the standards as per the PFA Rules, 1955. Thereafter, he sent the relevant papers to the Joint Commissioner Food and Drugs Administration to accord the prosecution sanction against respondent/accused. After receipt of prosecution sanction (consent), the PW-1 Bhagwat Bobde, the successor of complainant Gopal Pathak, fled the complaint against respondent for the respective charges under the PFA Act and its rules, as indicated above. 2] In response to the summons, respondent accused appeared before the learned Magistrate and pleaded not guilty. He denied the charges pitted against him. In order to bring home guilt of the respondent/accused, prosecution examined both the Food Inspectors PW-1 Bhagwat Bobade and PW-2 Gopal Pathak to prove the charges against respondent/accused. The prosecution also placed voluminous document on record including report of the public analyst (Exh.40). There are legal infrmities in the report of the public analyst. Therefore, it would unsafe to fasten the guilt on the respondent/accused.
texts.arguments: 3] Learned APP appearing for the appellant State of Maharashtra vehemently submits that the learned trial court did not appreciate the evidence on record in its proper perspective and State Of Maharashtra vs Prakash Rukman Kotalwar on 15 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43813926/ 2 committed error in acquittal of respondent accused in this court. The learned APP submits that there was due compliance of Rule 7(3) of {4} CRAPL 388.97.odt the PFA Act and, therefore, it would fallacious to discard the report of the public analyst. In the report of public analyst the date of analysis of item Badi-saunf was not shown but it would not fatal to the prosecution case. According to learned APP, it is not necessary for the complainant to prove that the food article seized was not ft for human consumption. He submits that sanctioning authority i.e. Joint Commissioner Food and Drugs Administration has considered the entire aspects of the crime and thereafter, accorded prosecution sanction (consent Exh.51). Therefore, the conclusion drawn by the learned Magistrate was erroneous, illegal and deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The respondent/accused is to be convicted for the charges pitted against him. The learned APP drawn attention to the evidence of PW-2 Food Inspector Gopal Pathak who has scrupulously followed the procedure prescribed under law for seizure and sealing of the articles and sending it to the authority of public analyst for analysis. 4] The learned counsel for respondent/accused assailed that the learned Magistrate has correctly appreciated the circumstances on record and drawn inference that respondent./accused could not be held guilty for the charges pitted against him on the basis of evidence adduced on record on behalf of prosecution. The learned counsel for respondent/accused submits that in the report of public analyst (Exh.40), the date of actual analysis of the item Badi-saunf was not mentioned. The item was sent to the public analyst on 2.2.1993 whereas, its report of analyais received to the complainant on 4.3.1993. According to learned counsel for respondent/accused it was imperative for the public analyst to mention the date on which the actual analysis of sample was taken place. There is legal lacuna in the present case. He relied upon the ratio laid down in the case of " State of Maharashtra Vs. Tirath Singha Saudagar Singh Khanuja" (1986) 1 FCA 166. {5} CRAPL 388.97.odt The learned counsel further raised objection that in the report of public analyst it was shown that sample was insect infested but it has not mentioned whether it was unft for human consumption. Moreover, the report does not make it clear that whether the extraneous non permitted colour detected from the sample was dangerous and hazardous for human consumption. The learned counsel contends that the entire prosecution case rests on the public analyst's report which is not in conformity with the provisions of law. Therefore, inference drawn by the learned trial court is just, proper and reasonable one. It does not warrant any interference. The learned Single Judge of this court Bench at Nagpur, in the case of "Tirath Singh" cited supra observed in para. 8 as under :- "Exh.31 is the report of Public Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur dated 3.9.1980. The Bombay High Court in Shaikh Hamid Vs. Dagu and another, 1979 (I) FAC 334, refused to interefere with acquittal in view of the absence of the date on the report of Analysit.
